solution: Probabilities are \(2k,k,2k,4k,k\) for \(X=0,1,2,3,4\). Sum \(=10k=1\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{1}{10}\). \(a=P(X<3)=2k+k+2k=5k=\dfrac{1}{2}\). \(b=P(2\le X<4)=P(2)+P(3)=2k+4k=6k=\dfrac{6}{10}=\dfrac{3}{5}\). Since \(\dfrac{1}{2}<\dfrac{3}{5}\), we have \(a<b\).

Total probability: \(\tfrac{1}{5} + A + B = 1 \Rightarrow A + B = \tfrac{4}{5}\).

\(E(X) = 30\cdot\tfrac{1}{5} + 10A + (-10)B = 4 \Rightarrow 6 + 10(A-B) = 4 \Rightarrow A - B = -\tfrac{1}{5}\).

Solving: \(A = \tfrac{3}{10},\; B = \tfrac{1}{2}\). Hence \(AB = \tfrac{3}{10}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2} = \tfrac{3}{20}\).

Non-negativity of all probabilities gives \(0\le p\le1\), so minimum \(p=0\). \(E(X)=0\cdot\dfrac{1+p}5+1\cdot\dfrac{2-2p}5+2\cdot\dfrac{2-p}5+3\cdot\dfrac{2p}5=\dfrac{6+2p}5\). Hence \(5E(X)=6+2p\); at \(p=0\), \(5E(X)=6\).

Sum of probabilities: \(\frac14+K+\frac14+\frac13 = 1 \Rightarrow K=\frac16\).
\(\mu = -3(\tfrac14)+0+1(\tfrac14)+\alpha(\tfrac13) = \frac{\alpha}{3}-\frac12\).
Using \(\sigma-\mu=2\) and \(\sigma^2 = E(X^2)-\mu^2\), solving gives \(\alpha=6\), \(\mu=\frac32\), so \(\sigma = 2+\mu = \frac72\).

text: A random variable X has the following probability distribution : -------------------------------------- \[X = x\] 1 2 3 4 -------------- ----- ----- ----- ----- \[P(X = x)\] 0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4 -------------------------------------- The mean and standard deviation of \(X\) are respectively

Arrange the following solutions according to decreasing order of osmotic pressure under similar condition of temperature and assuming complete dissociation. --------------------------------------------------------------- (I) 0.2 m KCl --------- ----------------------------------------------------- (II) \[0.3\text{ }m{MgSO}_{4}\] (III) \[0.1\text{ }m{BaCl}_{2}\] (IV) \[0.5\text{ }m{Al}_{2}\left( {SO}_{4} \right)_{3}\] ---------------------------------------------------------------
solution: Osmotic pressure \(\propto i\times m\) (total particle molality). KCl: \(0.2\times 2 = 0.4\); \(\mathrm{MgSO_4}\): \(0.3\times 2 = 0.6\); \(\mathrm{BaCl_2}\): \(0.1\times 3 = 0.3\); \(\mathrm{Al_2(SO_4)_3}\): \(0.5\times 5 = 2.5\). Decreasing order: \(2.5 > 0.6 > 0.4 > 0.3\), i.e. (IV) > (II) > (I) > (III).

solution: \(P(X=1)=P(H)=\dfrac12\); \(P(X=2)=\dfrac14\); \(P(X=3)=\dfrac18\); \(P(X=4)=P(\text{TTTH})+P(\text{TTTT})=\dfrac1{16}+\dfrac1{16}=\dfrac18\). The distribution \(\tfrac12,\tfrac14,\tfrac18,\tfrac18\) is option (D).

text: Given below are the critical temperatures of some of the gases: ------------------------------ ------------------ Gas Critical temperature (K) \[He\] 5.2 \[CH_{4}\] 190 \[CO_{2}\] 304.2 \[NH_{3}\] 405.5 ------------------------------ ------------------ The gas showing least adsorption on a definite amount of charcoal is:
solution: Physical adsorption of a gas on charcoal depends on how easily the gas liquefies, and the critical temperature measures exactly that: the higher the critical temperature, the more readily the gas condenses and the more strongly it is adsorbed. Ranking the given values, \(NH_{3}\) \((405.5)\) is adsorbed most and helium, with the lowest critical temperature of \(5.2\) K, is the hardest to liquefy and therefore the least adsorbed. The answer is option (A).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: (A) 2-Chloro-1,3-butadiene is chloroprene, whose free radical polymerisation gives neoprene, a synthetic rubber, so A-II. (B) Nylon 2-nylon 6 is the alternating polyamide of glycine and aminocaproic acid and is the standard example of a biodegradable polymer, so B-I. (C) Polyacrylonitrile is made by chain (addition) polymerisation of the vinyl monomer acrylonitrile, so C-IV. (D) Dacron (Terylene) is the condensation polymer of ethylene glycol and terephthalic acid, i.e. a polyester, so D-III. The match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

text:
Match List I with List II

| ------------ Example | ------------- ------------ ------------- | ------------- Hydride | LIST I ------------ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (A) | Electron deficient hydride | (I) | \[MgH_{2}\] |
| (B) | Electron rich hydride | (II) | \[HF\] |
| (C) | Electron precise hydride | (III) | \[B_{2}H_{6}\] |
| (D) | Saline hydride | (IV) | \[CH_{4}\] |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: (A) Electron deficient hydrides come from group 13, where the central atom has fewer electrons than needed for normal two-centre bonds; \(B_{2}H_{6}\), with its three-centre two-electron banana bonds, is the standard example, so A-III. (B) Electron rich hydrides come from groups 15 to 17 and carry lone pairs on the central atom; \(HF\) is such a hydride, so B-II. (C) Electron precise hydrides come from group 14 and have exactly the electrons needed for the bonds drawn; \(CH_{4}\) is tetrahedral and precise, so C-IV. (D) Saline (ionic) hydrides are formed by the strongly electropositive s-block metals; \(MgH_{2}\) is the only such compound listed, so D-I. The match is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

text: Match the column --------------------------- Column I Column II -------------- ------------ (i) Clouds (P) Gel (ii) Pumice (Q) stone Aerosols (iii) (R) Solid Cheese foam (iv) Shaving (S) cream Emulsion ---------------------------
solution: Classify each colloid by which phase is dispersed in which. Clouds are liquid droplets dispersed in a gas, i.e. an aerosol (Q). Pumice stone is gas trapped in a solid, a solid foam (R). Cheese is a liquid dispersed in a solid, a gel (P). Shaving cream, the remaining entry, pairs with (S). This gives (i)-Q, (ii)-R, (iii)-P, (iv)-S, option (A).

text: Match the column. ------------------------------------ Column I Column II ---------------- ------------------- 1. (A) Antibiotic Arsphenamine 2. Valium (B) Tranquilizer 3. Furacine (C) Antiseptic (D) Synthetic antihistamine ------------------------------------
solution: Arsphenamine, known as salvarsan, is the arsenic drug used against syphilis and is classed as the first effective antibiotic, so \(1\rightarrow A\). Valium (diazepam) is a benzodiazepine given to relieve anxiety and is a tranquilizer, so \(2\rightarrow B\). Furacine (nitrofurazone) is applied to wounds and burns to kill micro-organisms on living tissue, which makes it an antiseptic, so \(3\rightarrow C\). Option (A).
